name: A100 PCIe 80GB
notes: FP8/FP6/FP4 Tensor Core fields are null because Ampere does not support these precisions at all. No plain (non-Tensor-Core) FP16 vector figure is published. Unlike the SXM4 SKUs, PCIe NVLink is NOT a full multi-GPU fabric -- per NVIDIA's own footnote and the A100 80GB PCIe product brief, the 600 GB/s figure is achieved only between a bonded PAIR of PCIe cards using three physical NVLink bridge connectors (bridge, not native on-die fabric); nvlink_max_domain_size set to 2 to reflect this, versus 8 for the SXM4 baseboard SKUs. Memory bandwidth is stated as '1,935 GB/s' in the datasheet and as 'up to 1.94 TB/s' in the separate A100 80GB PCIe product brief -- same value, different rounding, not a real discrepancy. tdp_watts_max of 300W is both the default and maximum per the product brief's power table (300W default / 300W max / 150W min, i.e. software-configurable down to 150W but not up).

_sources.release_date: http://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-doubles-down-announces-a100-80gb-gpu-supercharging-worlds-most-powerful-gpu-for-ai-supercomputing (SC20, Nov 16 2020 -- separate later announcement for the 80GB variant, distinct from the original 40GB launch)
_sources.nvlink_bandwidth_gbps: https://www.nvidia.com/content/dam/en-zz/Solutions/Data-Center/a100/pdf/PB-10577-001_v02.pdf (A100 80GB PCIe product brief, Table 5: 3 NVLink bridges, 96 total Rx/Tx lanes, 50 Gbps/lane, 600 GB/s total)
_sources.memory_bandwidth_gbps: https://www.nvidia.com/content/dam/en-zz/Solutions/Data-Center/a100/pdf/nvidia-a100-datasheet-us-nvidia-1758950-r4-web.pdf; cross-checked against https://www.nvidia.com/content/dam/en-zz/Solutions/Data-Center/a100/pdf/PB-10577-001_v02.pdf which rounds the same value to 'up to 1.94 TB/s'
